result:
Lane finished. PR #209 is ready for review.

**What attempt 2 did:** no code. The implementation was complete and green on `b651d2b2e0`; attempt 1's only failure was ending with the PR in draft.

**Why attempt 1 didn't finish** — now in `docs/lanes/nightlytrunk/NOTES.md` and on the PR: it left an untracked `.ci-poll.sh` in the worktree, a 40-round `gh pr view` loop with `sleep 45` between rounds. It ran out of turns inside that loop, so it never reached `gh pr ready` and never posted a `waiting:` comment — from the outside, indistinguishable from a lane that gave up mid-change. The generalisable part: none of the four pre-ready items needed CI's answer, so the ~30 minutes of turns spent polling was exactly the budget the finish needed, and all four could have been done *before* the push that started the wait.

**Definition of done, verified:**

| item | state |
|---|---|
| preflight on the head | passed, and without needing `--allow-tracker` |
| `Files:` vs `git diff --name-status origin/master...HEAD` | 10 paths, exact match, both deletions marked |
| `docs/lanes/nightlytrunk/NOTES.md` | written, 202 lines, attempt record added |
| prediction | `none: analysis-only` — harness defect, moves no pixels, no arm |
| PR ready | `isDraft=false` |

CI on `b651d2b2e0` was `build` SUCCESS ×2 and `selftest` SUCCESS, with `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`. The one commit this attempt added (`22ab3d250b`) touches only the lane notes, so that green covers every executable line in the PR; CI is re-running on the new head as the gate of record.

One thing I have not confirmed and am not treating as blocking: I kicked off a local `bash docs/testing/jobs/selftest.sh` to re-check the "34 checks in fragment 87 / 1102 total" figure the notes and PR body claim, and it is still running. That figure was measured by attempt 1 and CI's own `selftest` check independently agrees the suite is green, so it gates nothing — I'll report the count if the run lands before this session ends. The two mislabelled releases are untouched, as the brief requires.
